MINUTES
  MALIBU PLANNING COMMISSION
  REGULAR MEETING
  SEPTEMBER 15. 2025
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  6:30 P.M.

CALL TO ORDER

  Vice Chair Riddick called the meeting to order at 6:31 pm.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Vice Chair Elizabeth Riddick and Commissioners Marni Kamins. John G.
  Mazza and Skylar Peak

  ABSENT: Chair Drew Leonard

  ALSO PRESENT: Trevor Rusin. Interim City Attorney: Yolanda Bundy. Community
  Development Director; Tatiana Holden. Assistant Public Works Director; Raneika
  Brooks. Principal Planner; Fletcher Allen. Associate Planner; Parker Davis, Media
  Technician; Gail Duncan. Administrative Assistant and Rebecca Evans: Recording
  Secretary

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Norm Haynie led the Pledge ofAllegiance.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Commissioner Mazza moved and Commissioner Kamins seconded a motion to
  approve the agenda. continuing Item No. 5.A. to the October 6. 2025 Regular
  Planning Commission meeting.

  The question was called and the motion carried 4—0. Chair Leonard absent.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  Recording Secretary Evans reported that the agenda l’or the meeting was properly posted
  on September 5, 2025; the amended agenda was properly posted on September 12. 2025.

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  None.

ITEM 2.  WRITTEN AND ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  None.

  COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT DIRECTOR REPORT

  Community Development Director Bundy announced the hiring of two additional
  contract planners to maintain quick turnaround times for like—for-like and like—for—
  like plus ten percent rebuilds. She also announced the birth of Principal Planner
  Eaton’s son Emery Thomas Kiyoshi Eaton and thanked Interim City Attorney
  Rusin for supporting the Planning Commission during Assistant City Attorney
  Martz’s absence. Community Development Director Bundy provided an update
  on rebuild statistics and upcoming events.

ITEM 3  CONSENT CALENDAR

ITEM 5  NEW PUBLIC HEARINGS

  Coastal Development Permit No. 25—009 — An application to install 19 new
  guardrails, 22 new or upgraded curb ramps. 6‘956 linear feet of new sidewalks,
  three new retaining walls, two realigned intersections, 42 new light poles, 15
  miles of new or upgraded bike lanes. a new California Highway Patrol pull—out,
  median reconstruction at various locations. and associated roadway improvements
  along Pacific Coast Highway within the Public Right—of—Way
  Locations:  Citywide. along Pacific Coast Highway within the Public Right—of—
  Way from Serra Road to the Ventura County border. located
  within the appealable coastal zone
  Owner:  California Department of Transportation
  Case Planner: Contract Planner Pisarkiewicz. AICP. 949—489-1442
  Recommended Action: Continue the item to the October 6. 2025 Regular
  Planning Commission meeting.

  This item was continued to the October 6. 2025 Regular Planning Commission
  meeting upon approval ofthe agenda.

  Coastal Development Permit No. 23—053 and Conditional Use Permit No. 23—005
  — An application for a 719 square foot modular building for the continued
  operation of a day labor hiring site operated by the Malibu Community Labor
  Exchange and associated development
  Location:  23525 Civic Center Way. not within the appealable coastal zone
  APN:  4458-022—906
  Owner:  County of Los Angeles
  Tenant:  Malibu Community Labor Exchange
  Case Planner: Associate Planner Allen. 456—2489. ext. 233
  Recommended Action: Adopt Planning Commission Resolution No. 25—71
  determining the project is categorically exempt from the California
  Environmental Quality Act. and approving Coastal Development Permit No. 23-
  053 for a new 719 square foot office building to allow for the continued operation
  of a day labor hiring site operated by the Malibu Community Labor Exchange.
  including Conditional Use Permit No. 23—005 for a philanthropic use. and
  recommending that the City Council approve an increase in floor area ratio from
  .193 to .195 in the Institutional zoning district located at 23525 Civic Center Way
  (County ofLos Angeles).

  Associate Planner Allen presented the staffreport.

  As there were no questions for staff. Vice Chair Riddick opened the public

  Speaker: None.

  As there were no speakers present. Vice Chair Riddick closed the public comment
  portion of the public hearing and returned the matter to the table for discussion.

  The Commission directed questions to staff.

MOTION  Commissioner Mazza moved and Vice Chair Riddick seconded a motion to adopt
  Planning Commission Resolution No. 25—7] determining the project is
  categorically exempt from the California Environmental Quality Act. and
  approving Coastal Development Permit No. 23—053 for a new 719 square foot
  office building to allow for the continued operation of a day labor hiring site
  operated by the Malibu Community Labor Exchange. including Conditional Use
  Permit No. 23—005 for a philanthropic use. and recommending that the City
  Council approve an increase in floor area ratio from .193 to .195 in the
  Institutional zoning district located at 23525 Civic Center Way (County of Los
  Angeles).

  The question was called and the motion carried 3—1. Commissioner Kamins
  dissenting and Chair Leonard absent.

  Coastal Development Permit No. 20—061. Variance No. 25—010, and Site Plan

  single-family residence with a basement. onsite wastewater treatment system.

  for construction on slopes steeper than 2.5 to 1 and a site plan review for

  APN:  4473-0l 1-045

  Case Planner: Principal Planner Brooks. 456—2489. ext. 276

  grading. retaining walls. landscaping. hardscape. an onsite wastewater treatment
  system. and associated development: including Variance No. 25—010 for

MOTION  Vice Chair Riddick moved and Commissioner Kamins seconded a motion to
  adopt Planning Commission Resolution No. 25—55. as amended. l) adding a
  second sentence to Condition No. 20 to state. “The second story deck shall install
  motion sensor lights“; 2) amending the second sentence of Condition No. 42 to
  state. “All vegetation including trees and fencing located within the front yard
  setback and the southern side yard setback up to the main structure shall be
  maintained at or below a height of 42 inches to preserve the ocean views from
  Encinal Canyon Road“; and 3) determining the project is categorically exempt
  from the California Environmental Quality Act. and approving Coastal
  Development Permit No. 20-061 for the construction of a new two-story. 3.800
  square foot single-family residence with a 1.100 square foot basement. pool.
  grading. retaining walls. landscaping. hardscape. an onsite wastewater treatment

  located in the Rural Residential. Two—Acre zoning district at 4510 Via Vicnta
  Street (Yaney and Hancock).
